tier_1_critical.clinical_definition: Errors directly risking catastrophic diagnostic failure, delayed emergency intervention, or incorrect surgical intervention.
criteria: Failure to report an acute life-threatening pathology (e.g. acute cholecystitis, abdominal aortic aneurysm > 5cm, active hemoperitoneum)
Laterality transposition (confusing Right Kidney pathology with Left Kidney)
Hallucinating normal anatomy for a surgically absent or excised organ
Inventing non-existent critical masses or severe conditions

tier_2_major.clinical_definition: Errors altering clinical staging, leading to unwarranted secondary diagnostic imaging, or significant measurement unit distortion.
criteria: Metric dimension distortion by factor of 10 (e.g. reporting 4.5 cm instead of 4.5 mm)
Misclassifying solid vs cystic lesion (e.g. reporting a complex renal cyst as simple fluid cyst)
Omission of positive sonographic Murphy's sign in symptomatic biliary dictation
Failure to report loss of corticomedullary differentiation in renal disease

tier_3_minor.clinical_definition: Semantic, typographical, or non-actionable stylistic deviations that do not change patient management.
criteria: Variations in descriptive adjectives (e.g. 'mild steatosis' vs 'minimal steatosis')
Synonym substitution for anatomical landmarks (e.g. 'hepatorenal fossa' vs 'Morison pouch')
Minor punctuation or template layout formatting differences
